notes: Vatican City publishes no health/anthropometric statistics for its ~800 residents (clergy, religious and lay officials, predominantly older males); WHO GHO has no VAT rows for NCD_BMI_30C/NCD_BMI_30A or smoking indicators (checked via API filter SpatialDim eq 'VAT').
All health fields derived from anchor Italy (IT) values as verified in countries-database.json: residents are Italian citizens living in Rome with equivalent healthcare, diet and lifestyle.

Derived values = Italy's: F height 161 cm / weight 65 kg / BMI 25 / obesity 21% / smoking 18% / LE 86 y; M height 173 cm / weight 77 kg / BMI 25.6 / obesity 18.5% / smoking 28% / LE 82 y; obesityRate 21%, smokingRate 18%.

Anthropometrics and obesity from the national measured survey: Wallis & Futuna STEPS 2019 (WHO/ADSWF, N=1136 measured adults 18-69) - mean height F 165.5 cm / M 176.8 cm; mean weight F 95.9 kg / M 103.8 kg; mean BMI F 34.8 / M 33.0 kg/m2; obesity (BMI>=30) F 73.7% / M 66.7%, both sexes 70.4%.
Smoking (current tobacco use, STEPS 2019): men 53.6%, women 29.4%, overall 40.7% - among the highest tobacco prevalences in the Pacific.

Life expectancy: UN WPP 2023 via OWID grapher gives total e0 = 78.6 for WLF (no WHO GHO rows exist for WLF). Sex split derived using the female-male gap of French Pacific territories in the DB (French Polynesia 4.7 y, New Caledonia 4.9 y): F ~81.0 / M ~76.2.

Values are far above metropolitan France's (anchor FR); real territorial survey data used instead of French derivation because Wallisian health profile matches neighbouring Polynesian populations (Samoa/Tonga obesity 40-50%+).
Only life expectancies were missing; all other health fields (heights, weights, BMI, obesity, smoking) already populated and consistent with Morocco.
No WHO GHO or World Bank rows exist for ESH (checked GHO filter SpatialDim eq 'ESH' for WHOSIS_000001, NCD_BMI_30C/A and smoking indicators - zero rows).

Life expectancy: UN WPP 2023 via OWID grapher gives total e0 = 71.4 for Western Sahara. Sex split derived from anchor Morocco's gap in the DB (F 77.8 / M 73.3, gap 4.5 y): F ~73.7 / M ~69.2, i.e. total 71.4 +/- half the Moroccan sex gap.
Scaled-from-Morocco approach per repair brief anchor rule 'Western Sahara -> MA'; territory has no separate civil health registry.
